scope: - Ref `configure` values the plan depends on: 16 rows, a tick period of 1 s (rate group 1 Hz) and a default table file that the plan overrides with `TABLE_FILE`, for both `seqSched` and `seqSchedB`.
- UUT: `Svc.SeqScheduler`, `lestarch-autobot/fprime` branch `seq-scheduler`; SHA recorded in the manifest.
- Test fixture: `Ref.TimeBaseSetter`, instance `timeBaseSetter`, between every component's time port and `posixTime`.

- Deployment: `TestDeploymentsProject/Ref`, the repository's full reference deployment, with `seqSched` -> `schedSeq` (`Svc.CmdSequencer`) and `seqSchedB` -> `schedSeqB`, both schedulers on the 1 Hz rate group, their channels in a new `SeqSched` telemetry packet.
- Bench: native Linux `Ref` and `fprime-gds` on the session VM, one file system shared by the image and the harness; no hardware, no power control. Restart = stop and start the `Ref` process.
- Ground system: `fprime-gds` from the UUT's `requirements.txt`; sequences built with `fprime-seqgen`; table files written by `Svc/SeqScheduler/scripts/seq_schedule_table.py`.

- Sequencer idle (require on every test) = every `CS_SequenceLoaded` or `CS_PortSequenceStarted` of this start of `Ref` in the record is followed by a complete or cancel event of the same sequencer before the test's opening marker.

- Parameters at plan values (require on every test) = for each parameter, the last `*_PRM_SET` command of this start in the record, with its `OpCodeCompleted`, carries the plan value, or none was sent since the start (the image starts from the plan's parameter file).
- Out of scope: `Svc.WasmSequencer` and FPy sequencers as the attached sequencer; uplink of table and sequence files (written directly to the shared file system).
entry_gates: - The harness sends each command only after the completion of the previous one is recorded, so the component queue (size 10) is never filled by commands.
- Unit tests of `Svc/SeqScheduler` pass with every row of the SDD unit-test list implemented; unit tests of the fixture `Ref/TimeBaseSetter` pass.
- `Ref` built from the manifest SHA; `fth verify-plan plan.json --tests .` passes.
- Marker round-trip: `CdhCore.cmdDisp.CMD_NO_OP_STRING("100")` logged as `Received a NO-OP string=100` (L0-1).
- Event budget: the busiest window (L2-14) raises under 50 events in 60 s; Ref's TCP downlink has no rate limit.

- Sequence files built and present: `short.bin` and `short2.bin` = two `CdhCore.cmdDisp.CMD_NO_OP` records, relative delay 0, no wait, run time under 2 s; `long.bin` = `CMD_NO_OP`, a 20 s relative wait, `CMD_NO_OP`. `missing.bin` absent. The dry run confirms the run times.

- A time base override does not stop the image: confirmed in L0-2, which runs short.bin under the override, before any other test. `Fw::Time` comparison across bases is `INCOMPARABLE`, not an assert (`Fw/Time/Time.cpp`), but a `Svc.CmdSequencer` wait started in one base never expires in another: no test changes the override while `long.bin` runs.
- Run order: L0-1, L0-2 first; L2-5 and L2-11 in the same start of `Ref` as the first report of their time base; L3-1 (restart) after them. The order is fixed, not drawn.
levels: L0 provenance/feasibility · L2 functional · L3 persistence/restart · L5 fault paths · L6 negative controls · L7 final state for independent verification. No L4: the component has no performance requirement.

decision_log: 1. 2026-11-16 designer — marker = `CdhCore.cmdDisp.CMD_NO_OP_STRING` with a decimal id; Ref has the command and 40-character strings.
2. 2026-11-16 designer — a dedicated `Svc.CmdSequencer` per scheduler instance (SDD §3.5); `cmdSeq` stays the ground's sequencer.
3. 2026-11-16 designer — table and sequence files are written to the shared file system, not uplinked; planted faults are therefore command rewrites and insertions only.

4. 2026-11-16 designer — relative-row tests read elapsed ticks through `NextTimeDue` of a far-future row (time due less the sample's own time is the delay remaining) to place the row's due time, and check that elapsed value against an origin recorded outside the scheduler: the bench's process start time (L2-4, L3-1) or the record's first `TimeBaseSet` event for the base (L2-5, L2-11). Review round 1, TD-01.
5. 2026-11-16 designer — coverage thresholds left at the skill baselines.
6. 2026-11-16 designer — `Ref.TimeBaseSetter` is the plan's helper component, with unit tests of its own; superseded in part by decision 8.

7. 2026-11-16 designer — redundancy: every requirement with system coverage has two or more covering tests, at least one of them carrying no planted fault another covering test carries. Second tests reuse the second scheduler instance (L2-10, L2-13, L2-14, L5-4) and a second time base (L2-12) rather than repeat a test. REQ-001 and REQ-024 need a second restart test to be redundant; they are verified by unit test and listed under not-covered.

8. 2026-11-16 human (Michael Starch, 12:55 PST) — one SDD, for the component asked for: `Svc.SeqScheduler` is the only unit under test. `Ref.TimeBaseSetter` is a test fixture of the `Ref` deployment with no SDD and no requirements of its own; its unit tests and L0-2 show it fit for use. Closes TD-09 as a helper; the plan moved to `Svc/SeqScheduler/test/int`.

9. 2026-11-16 designer — `FSW time + N s` means the seconds of an event received at most 1 s before the command is sent, used with the row's commanded time base; an override leaves seconds unchanged (L0-2). Review round 1, TD-14.

10. 2026-11-16 designer — planted faults now reach an absence check (`early_override`, L2-3 W1), the second instance (`cross_instance`, L2-10) and a fault-path test (`missing_file_present`, L5-1); `wrong_seq` is classed `stimulus`. Whether a `precedes` or latency predicate with an absent operand reports FAIL or UNVERIFIED is confirmed with a replay vector in the dry run before sealing (TD-21).

11. 2026-11-16 designer — L5-2 expectations follow `Svc.CmdSequencer` as read: a run refused while busy is answered at once with `seqDone(EXECUTION_ERROR)`. SDD §7 describes a sequencer that stays silent; the wording is raised at Approve SDD, not edited here.

12. 2026-11-16 designer — review round 2: sequence file contents and run times fixed in entry gate 5 (TD-22); L0-2 waits for `short.bin` to complete before clearing the override and requires a record from each of five instances inside the span (TD-22, TD-24); the two common requires are defined from the record (TD-23).

13. 2026-11-16 designer — instance names are the dictionary's qualified names: `Ref.` for the deployment's own instances, `CdhCore.`, `FileHandling.`, `DataProducts.`, `ComCcsds.` for subtopology instances (read from the topology model).

14. 2026-11-16 designer — review round 3 (closed by the author after the last review of the bound; unverified): downlink-loss guard uses channels that exist in Ref's packets, `CdhCore.events.EventsDropped` and the two `ComCcsds.comQueue` drop channels, to be confirmed against the built dictionary in the L0 bench check (TD-26); L0-2 checks the time tag of the component's own event (TD-27); helper and require strings use qualified names (TD-28).

15. 2026-11-16 human (Michael Starch, 15:16 PST) and designer — plan regenerated for the reworked requirements (48 rows): no completion time-out (old L5-2 and L5-4 replaced by tests of edits and a load during a running sequence); busy policies WAIT_FOR_RUNNING, CANCEL_RUNNING, SKIP_WHEN_RUNNING (L2-6, L2-7, L2-8, L2-13, L2-14); one SET_ROW command; `SeqRun`, `SeqDoneUnexpected`, `RowSkippedBusy`, `RowSet` events; `NextTimeDue` and `RowsWaiting` channels. Entry 11 no longer applies. Requirement numbers in entries 1-14 are those of the first gate.

16. 2026-11-16 designer — reopened review round 1: `wrong_seq` no longer applies to L7-1 (a stimulus fault must leave the final state right); latency bounds on tests with two windows are helper checks scoped to their window, not unscoped metrics; L2-1 loads T-FIELDS, whose rows 14 and 15 hold a non-default value in every field; REQ-005 traces to L3-1 and L7-1, where a load replaces edited content. The GDS rendering of a `Fw.TimeValue` argument (the `RowSet` pattern, the `row_time_late` argument form, the row times read back in L7-1) is confirmed in the dry run before sealing (RT-15), with TD-21. A 'run no earlier than' helper holds when the row is not run in the window; a 'run no later than' helper fails; both are confirmed in the same dry run (RT-17).

17. 2026-11-18 human (Michael Starch, 09:07 PST) — the per-row late policy proposed on 2026-11-17 is withdrawn: a row found more than `LATE_TOLERANCE_SEC` past due is skipped, as an operations constraint. `RowLate` and `RowSkippedBusy` are WARNING_LO; the query port argument is `i`. The plan is the one reviewed on 2026-11-16, with REQ-SeqScheduler-042 given as Integration Test.

18. 2026-11-18 human (Michael Starch, 09:20 PST) — `TicksDropped` telemetry and the queue-overflow hooks are removed: `run` counts ticks and queues at most one tick message; any other queue overflow is the framework assertion.

19. 2026-11-18 human (Michael Starch, 14:32 and 14:35 PST) — table length, default table file and tick period come from `configure` (no `TICK_PERIOD_USEC` parameter, REQ-048 removed); a missing table file at start-up gives an empty table (unit test); disabled-row skips emit `RowSkippedDisabled`; `EXECUTING` state; `SET_ENABLED` and `REPORT_ACTIVE_ROW` (L2-15, L2-16 added); requirements 051 to 059 added, seven of them verified by unit test only.

20. 2026-11-18 human (Michael Starch, 16:12 PST) — row state is not saved: every loaded row is PENDING and a past row is skipped with no event on the first tick after a load (L2-1, L3-1, L7-1 reworked; REQ-024 removed; REQ-056 now has system coverage); a failed load leaves an empty table that commands can fill (REQ-043 and `NO_TABLE` removed; L5-1, L5-3 reworked; L5-1 says truncated, not short); due rows are handled by time due, then index, and a due CANCEL_RUNNING row skips every due row ahead of it (REQ-060, `RowSkippedByCancel`; L2-13 reworked); a relative row's time due is its origin's system time plus its time (REQ-046, REQ-061).

21. 2026-11-18 human (Michael Starch, 16:24 PST) and designer — the due rows are held in the existing `Fw::ExternalRedBlackTreeSet`; tests of several rows due with a later CANCEL_RUNNING row, and with the cancel row between other due rows, are added (L2-7 and L2-13 reworked, REQ-060 now has system coverage; unit tests CancelLastOfSeveralDue, CancelBetweenDue, TwoCancelsDue).
